body_markdown:
# Introduction

This quiz reviews common simple and continuous tense forms. Read each sentence carefully and look for time clues such as every day, yesterday, now and tomorrow.

## Section A: Choose the correct option

**1. She ___ to school every day.**

A. go B. goes C. going

**2. They ___ cricket now.**

A. are playing B. play C. played

**3. I ___ him yesterday.**

A. meet B. meets C. met

**4. We ___ tomorrow.**

A. will travel B. travelled C. travelling

**5. He ___ TV when I called.**

A. watches B. was watching C. watch

**6. I ___ my homework already.**

A. have finished B. finish yesterday C. finishing

**7. The sun ___ in the east.**

A. rise B. rises C. rising

**8. She ___ dinner at the moment.**

A. is cooking B. cooked every day C. cook

**9. They ___ here last week.**

A. are B. was C. were

**10. I think it ___ rain later.**

A. will B. did C. is yesterday

## Section B: Complete the sentences

11. He usually ___ (drink) tea in the morning.  
12. We ___ (watch) a film now.  
13. She ___ (visit) Pune last month.  
14. I ___ (call) you tomorrow.  
15. They ___ (work) when the lights went out.

## Answer key

1. B — goes  
2. A — are playing  
3. C — met  
4. A — will travel  
5. B — was watching  
6. A — have finished  
7. B — rises  
8. A — is cooking  
9. C — were  
10. A — will  
11. drinks  
12. are watching  
13. visited  
14. will call  
15. were working

## Score guide

- 13–15: Very good. Review only the errors.
- 10–12: Good progress. Practise the tense forms you missed.
- 0–9: Revise present simple, present continuous, past simple and future simple before repeating.

## Learning tip

Do not guess from the verb alone. Identify when the action happens and whether it is a habit, completed event or action in progress.

faq.question: Which tenses should beginners learn first?
faq.answer: Start with present simple, present continuous, past simple and future simple.

faq.question: What words help identify tense?
faq.answer: Words such as every day, now, yesterday and tomorrow can provide useful clues.

faq.question: Should I memorise tense names only?
faq.answer: No. Practise making your own sentences and choosing verbs in context.
